title: Asparagus, canned, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Canned asparagus consists of selected spears that are blanched and sealed in airtight jars without any added fat. The process retains most of the vegetable’s nutrients, its delicate flavor, and a pleasant bite.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Asparagus has been cultivated for over 2,000 years and is one of the oldest known vegetables.
Canning extends its shelf life to 2–3 years while preserving quality.
In the United States, canned asparagus ranks among the top ten most consumed canned vegetables.
Canned spears are a convenient shortcut for soups, stews, and salads.
Asparagus is rich in antioxidants, especially glutathione.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate supports DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides roughly 20 kcal, making it ideal for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Glutathione and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to asparagus.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned vegetables often contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Food interactions
items.content: Large amounts of asparagus can increase vitamin K levels, potentially affecting anticoagulant medication.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat the spears cold in salads, toss them into pasta, omelets, or soups. Open the jar, drain the liquid, and if desired, quickly heat on a skillet or in the microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct light. After opening, transfer the asparagus to an airtight container and keep refrigerated, using within 3–4 days.
